_description: eval_v1 IDs whose gold answer is suspected to be wrong by >=2 decades based on first-principles spot-check. Excluded from headline fp_score; reported separately. Investigate upstream realFP source before reinstating.
_spot_check_method: manual first-principles re-derivation on random sample stratified by source
_addendum_during_baseline: realFP:test:1 also looks wrong: gold=0.23 for 'fraction of sun's energy intercepted by earth' — true value ~4.5e-10 from Earth-cross-section / sphere-at-1AU geometry. Kept out-of-file for now pending broader audit; see experiments/runs.jsonl for per-item evidence.

eval_v1.question: How dense is the Milky Way galaxy in terms of stars per cubic light year?
eval_v1.reason: MW has ~2e11 stars in a disk of volume ~1e13 ly^3, giving ~10^-2 stars/ly^3. Gold is ~9 decades too large; may be stored inverted or unit bug.

eval_v1.question: What mass of neutrinos leave the sun every second?
eval_v1.reason: Solar neutrino luminosity ~8e24 W; at ~0.1 eV/c^2 per neutrino and ~5e37 neutrinos/s emitted, total rest mass ~10 kg/s. Mass-energy equivalent of neutrino flux ~9e7 kg/s. Gold off by ~20 decades.

eval_v1.question: How much energy is needed to raise sea levels by 5 feet over 50 years?
eval_v1.reason: Ice melt to raise sea 1.5m requires ~2e23 J; over 50 y = 1.6e9 s gives ~1e14 W. Gold ~5e8 W is off by ~5-6 decades.

eval_v1.question: If I were going to go to the moon and wanted to leave proof I was there that could be seen from earth, how big would the proof have to be?
eval_v1.reason: Naked-eye angular resolution ~1 arcmin → ~110 km at lunar distance → min area ~1e4 km^2. Gold of 1.1e7 km^2 exceeds moon's visible hemisphere area (~2e7 km^2) — implausible.
